name: live-quiet-and-empty-recovery
detail: Two real foreground checkpoints returned 0 without wakes. Ordinary downtime was retired on the same generation; the singleton lock was released.

name: live-durable-recovery-ack
detail: A real queued wake resurfaced once, survived a second quiet checkpoint unchanged, and was removed only by the drain acknowledgement printed by the product.

name: live-checkpoint-signal
detail: Writing a real status file closed the foreground checkpoint with one signal line, exit 0, and a durable wake row.

name: live-interrupted-startup
detail: Interrupted real startup returned failure in 2.79s (1s checkpoint plus 2s cleanup, below the 5s kill grace), retained the identity-bound lock, and never published a beacon.

name: live-owned-stall
detail: The real owned arm returned nonzero for a watcher stalled on the recovery lock, printed the already-delivered signal exactly once, and retained the durable queue byte for byte.

name: live-attached-stall
detail: The real attached arm returned nonzero for a watcher stalled on the recovery lock, printed the already-delivered signal exactly once, and retained the durable queue byte for byte.

name: live-host-quiet-boundary
detail: The opted-in real Codex primary ran a host checkpoint to its park boundary, returned quiet exit 0, and left no watcher singleton.

name: live-host-attended-successors
detail: Two attended wakes from a real Codex primary reached main exactly once, each retained a live successor across acknowledgement, and the second host took over the previous cycle. Explicit stop succeeded.

name: live-host-predecessor-delivery
detail: Replacement activation after a real host KILL returned 1, reported forced-cleanup failure, retained the same watcher identity, and surfaced its delivered wake once.

name: live-host-preconfirmation-retirement
detail: Replacement activation after a real host KILL returned 1, reported forced-cleanup failure, retained the same watcher identity, and did not accept interrupted pre-beacon startup as healthy.

name: live-forced-kill-checkpoint
detail: A real watcher frozen with SIGSTOP during contended shutdown outlasted the kill grace: the real checkpoint returned 137 after 11.33s, printed the forced-KILL diagnostic, and retained stale lock evidence.

name: live-startup-refusal
detail: A real arm with an unusable startup confirmation budget failed before publishing a singleton, with its typed launch diagnostic.

name: live-codex-away-checkpoint-note
detail: Real Codex detection: away entry without a watcher prints the foreground-checkpoint warning and creates no cycle; a healthy real foreground checkpoint suppresses it; quiet entry does not print the away warning.

name: live-interrupted-takeover
detail: The interrupted take-over arm stopped the original watcher while still owning the handed-off recovery lock; it emitted a cleanup-failure diagnostic after the external recovery-lock holder had released. taker exit=143; original arm exit=143
